title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 3
paragraphs: So they advised, but he did not follow their counsel, for a great desire had taken hold of him to capture Athens a second time — partly from obstinacy and partly because he meant to signal to the king at Sardis, by beacon-fires through the islands, that he held Athens. Even this time, however, he did not find the Athenians there when he came to Attica; he was informed that most of them were either on Salamis or on the ships, and he captured the city finding it deserted. Now the king's capture of the city had taken place ten months before this later expedition of Mardonius against it.
